title: The sp Hybridization of Tin Single Atoms for Dendrite-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
text: Graphene oxide was used as a 2D support to anchor atomically dispersed Sn single atoms. The Sn precursor solution was freeze-dried and then annealed at 400 C for 3 h under Ar to obtain Sn SAs/G. ICP-OES showed 2.93 wt% Sn and BET showed a specific surface area of 543 m2 g-1. XANES and XPS indicated a +4 valence state of Sn. In situ TEM showed uniform planar Na deposition on Sn SAs/G, whereas Na dendrites appeared on graphene and Na nanoparticles formed on Ni SAs/G. In half cells with 1 m NaPF6/diglyme electrolyte, Sn SAs/G showed an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.8% for 200 cycles at 1 mA cm-2 and 1 mAh cm-2. A symmetric Sn SAs/G-Na battery cycled for 600 h at 4 mA cm-2 and showed 40 mV overpotential at 8 mA cm-2. A full battery Na3V2(PO4)3 || Sn SAs/G-Na delivered 67 mAh g-1 at 20 C and retained 91% capacity after 500 cycles. DFT calculations showed that Sn SAs/G had a Na adsorption energy of -1.49 eV and that the 5s2 5p2 configuration of Sn favored planar Na3 cluster growth.
